title: CLR/1/2014 of Satish Kumar Chawla Vs Smt. Ranjana Pathania AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Civil Revision No. 1 of 2014
Satish Kumar Chawla Ö..Plaintiff/Revisionist.
Versus
Smt. Ranjana Pathania & another
 ......Ö.Defendants/Respondents.
Present:
Mr. Pawan Mishra, Advocate for the plaintiff/revisionist.
Honíble Alok Singh, J (Oral).
Plaintiff-revisionist instituted J.S.C.C. Suit No.
30 of 2012 in the court of J.S.C.C., District Dehradun
against the defendants/ respondents herein, for eviction
of the tenants/respondents herein, and for recovery of
arrears of rent. Suit so filed by the plaintiff/ revisionist
herein, was decreed ex parte vide judgment and decree
dated 14.3.2013 passed by J.S.C.C./A.D.J., Rishikesh,
District Dehradun. Plaintiff/ revisionist herein, thereafter
moved an application for execution of the ex parte decree
dated 14.3.2013, whereupon notices were issued to the
respondents.
Having acquired knowledge about the
execution of ex parte judgment and decree passed
against them, defendants/respondents moved an
application under Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C. for setting
aside ex parte judgment and decree dated 14.3.2013 on
13.9.2013. It is specifically stated in the affidavit, filed in
support of the application for setting aside ex parte
judgment and decree, that earlier suit was instituted and
pending before the J.S.C.C./District Judge, Dehradun,
however, after the creation of the Court of Additional
District Judge at Rishikesh, case was transferred to the

2
Court of J.S.C.C./A.D.J., Rishikesh but no notice was
ever sent to or received either by the defendants or by
their counsel about the transfer of the case and next date
fixed in the Court of J.S.C.C./A.D.J., Rishikesh. It is
further stated that defendants remained under bona fide
impression that they would be served with fresh notice by
the transferee court about the transfer of the case and
the date fixed before the transferee court as required by
Rule 89-A of the General Rules (Civil), 1957, therefore, ex
parte judgment and decree without service of notice
about the transfer of case, as required under Rule 89-A
of the General Rules (Civil), 1957 is liable to be set aside.
An application was moved by the defendants/
respondents herein, under Section 17 of the Provincial
Small Cause Courts Act before the court seeking
permission of the court to furnish security of the entire
decreetal amount, as required by Section 17. Learned
trial court, vide impugned order dated 4.12.2013, was
pleased to allow the application moved under Section 17
of the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act permitting the
defendants to furnish security of the decreetal
amount. Consequently, defendants/ respondents herein,
submitted security bond before the learned court below
which was accepted by the learned court below vide order
dated 9.12.2013. Feeling aggrieved, plaintiff/revisionist
herein, preferred the present revision under Section 25 of
the Provincial Small Cause Courts Act, 1887 assailing
the order dated 4.12.2013, whereby application moved by
the defendants/respondents herein, was allowed.
Mr. Pawan Mishra, learned counsel appearing
for the plaintiff/revisionist herein, vehemently argued
that application under Section 17 of the Act ought to
have been moved either prior to the application for

3
setting aside decree or at least along with the application
for setting aside the decree. He further submitted that
application under Section 17 of the Act should not be
allowed to be moved after filing of the original application
under Order 9 Rule 13 C.P.C., therefore, non filing of the
application under Section 17 of the Act either prior to the
filing of the application seeking setting aside ex parte
decree or along with application seeking setting aside ex
parte decree is fatal.
Perusal of the ordersheet of the learned trial
court would reveal that no reply was filed by the
plaintiff/revisionist herein, to the application for setting
aside ex parte judgment and decree and application
seeking permission to furnish security in terms of Section
17 of the Act was moved by the defendants/respondents
herein, on 2.12.2013 i.e. prior to filing of the reply to the
application for setting aside ex parte decree.
This is now settled position of law that every
lis, as far as possible, should be decided after giving
sufficient opportunities to both the sides and, ordinarily,
walkover should not be allowed to one side.
In view of the peculiar facts and circumstances
of the case that application seeking permission to furnish
security in terms of Section 17 of Provincial Small Cause
Courts Act was moved by the defendants/respondents
herein, prior to filing of the reply to the application for
setting aside ex parte decree, I do not find any reason to
disturb the judicial discretion exercised by the learned
trial court. Therefore, I am not inclined to entertain this
revision.

4
Consequently, revision is dismissed at the
admission stage itself.
CLMA No. 1294 of 2014 also stands disposed
of accordingly.
(Alok Singh, J.)
 26.2.2014
Avneet
